questions.cardText:
[Physics] Under which condition can water boil and freeze simultaneously?
A. At 32 °F (0 °C) with intense vibration
B. At 122 °F (50 °C) and high pressure
C. At 32 °F and low pressure
Answer: C. This phenomenon occurs at the triple point, where water exists simultaneously as a solid, liquid, and gas.
questions.de: Wie heißt der Punkt – knapp über 0 °C und bei sehr niedrigem Druck –, an dem Wasser gleichzeitig sieden und gefrieren kann, weil es zugleich fest, flüssig und gasförmig vorliegt?
questions.en: What is the name of the point — just above 0 °C and at very low pressure — at which water can boil and freeze at the same time, existing simultaneously as a solid, liquid and gas?

timeline.labelEn: James Thomson, brother of Lord Kelvin, first uses the term "triple point"
timeline.labelDe: James Thomson, Bruder von Lord Kelvin, verwendet erstmals den Begriff „Tripelpunkt“

questions.notes: The card's "32 °F and low pressure" is approximate: water's triple point is 0.01 °C (32.018 °F) at a vapour pressure of 611.657 Pa.

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which of the following animals has been observed to laugh?
A. Platypus
B. Rat
C. Capybara
Answer: B. Rats can emit high-pitched vocalizations that resemble laughter when they are tickled, suggesting that they have a capacity for play and joy similar to what is seen in humans.
questions.de: Welches Nagetier stößt hohe 50-kHz-Ultraschallrufe aus, die an Lachen erinnern, wenn es von Menschen gekitzelt wird?
questions.en: Which rodent emits high-pitched, 50-kHz ultrasonic calls resembling laughter when it is tickled by humans?

timeline.labelEn: Jaak Panksepp and Jeff Burgdorf publish their study of 50-kHz "laughter" chirps in tickled rats
timeline.labelDe: Jaak Panksepp und Jeff Burgdorf veröffentlichen ihre Studie über 50-kHz-„Lach“-Rufe gekitzelter Ratten

questions.notes: Great apes also produce laughter-like vocalizations when tickled; the question asks specifically about the rodent with ultrasonic calls.
